newsitem.title: UK: Russia debt price surges on debt, bond news.
newsitem.headline: Russia debt price surges on debt, bond news.

text.p: News on Russia's old and new borrowing sent prices of its debt sharply higher on Monday.
The rest of the emerging debt market was fairly quiet, though Bulgaria lost ground again.
Russia's deputy finance minister announced earlier that the government would launch a one billion mark Eurobond in early March as part of about $3 billion to be issued in Eurobonds this year.
Mikhail Kasyanov also told Reuters in Moscow that the debt rescheduling deal with the London Club would close by early April.
"People had thought there would be a further delay. I'm quite encourage," one Russian debt trader said.
"There's been quite a significant change in the view of Russia in the past week. (Russian President) Boris (Yeltsin) seems to be holding up, and other news is quite good," he said.
The Kremlin said Yeltsin, who met French President Jacques Chirac on Sunday, would have a limited number of meetings this week.
Dollar Vneshekonombank debt jumped 1-3/8 points to 81-1/8 cents in the dollar to its highest level in more than two months.
Bulgaria, the market's most volatile asset this year, put in a less robust performance, dropping close to a point, following Friday's sharp rise in New York.
